topics.name: Story elements
misconceptions: Learners mix up characters and setting, or think the plot is only the end of the story.

topics.name: Nouns, verbs and adjectives
misconceptions: Learners think every describing word is an adjective, or that verbs are only action words and miss words like is and was.

topics.name: Writing a recount
misconceptions: Learners write in the present tense or jump around in time instead of telling events in the order they happened.

topics.name: Show and tell talks
misconceptions: Learners read from notes the whole time or speak for longer than one minute and do not let the class ask questions.

topics.name: Poems and rhyme
misconceptions: Learners think every line of a poem must rhyme, or clap the beat instead of the rhythm of the words.

topics.name: Capital letters and punctuation
misconceptions: Learners put capital letters in the middle of sentences or forget to put a full stop at the end of a sentence.

topics.name: Writing a paragraph
misconceptions: Learners write one long sentence or start a new line for every sentence instead of grouping related ideas together.

topics.name: Listening to instructions
misconceptions: Learners miss a step when following spoken steps, or give steps to a partner in the wrong order.

topics.name: Writing linked paragraphs
misconceptions: Learners write two separate paragraphs that do not connect, or forget to use joining words such as first, then and finally.

topics.name: Reading for information
misconceptions: Learners copy sentences straight from the text instead of answering in their own words, or they miss the headings and captions.

topics.name: Past, present and future tenses
misconceptions: Learners add -ed to every verb for the past tense, even irregular verbs, or they mix tenses in one piece of writing.

topics.name: Writing a friendly letter
misconceptions: Learners forget the address, date or greeting, or they write the letter like a story instead of a letter.

topics.name: Reading a longer story
misconceptions: Learners only write about what happens and do not record favourite parts or new words in their reading journal.

topics.name: Prepositions and conjunctions
misconceptions: Learners confuse prepositions with conjunctions, or they use and for every sentence instead of but or because.

topics.name: Writing a story
misconceptions: Learners forget to include a problem in the story, or they write the ending before the middle.

topics.name: Class debate
misconceptions: Learners shout over each other or only speak for their own team and do not listen to the other side.

leftOut.name: Writing a formal essay
leftOut.reason: It is a Grade 7 skill and is not taught in Grade 5 this year.
